title: Doomsday
tagline: Find the weekday of any date in your head.

tile.title: Doomsday
tile.blurb: Learn to find the weekday of any date in your head.

learn.intro: Every year, a handful of easy-to-remember dates (4/4, 6/6, 8/8 …) all fall on the same weekday: the year's doomsday. Find that weekday, find the nearest doomsday date in the month, and count. Four steps:
learn.step1Body: Each century has an anchor weekday. They repeat every 400 years: Tue, Sun, Fri, Wed.
learn.step2Body: Take the last two digits of the year (T).
learn.oddRule4: Take the remainder when dividing by 7.
learn.oddRule5: Subtract it from 7 (7 − 7 = 0). Count that many days forward from the century anchor.
learn.step3Title: 3. The doomsday date in the month
learn.step3Body: These dates always fall on the year's doomsday:
learn.evenMonths: Even months: 4/4, 6/6, 8/8, 10/10, 12/12 — the day equals the month.
learn.nineToFive: "I work 9-to-5 at the 7-Eleven": 9 May (9/5) and 5 September, 11 July and 7 November.
learn.janFeb: January: the 3rd (the 4th in leap years). February: the last day — 28th (29th).
learn.step4Body: Subtract the doomsday date from your date. Throw away whole weeks (7, 14, 21, 28 days land on the same weekday) and count what's left forwards (or backwards if negative).
learn.leapBody: Divisible by 4 is a leap year — except whole centuries, unless divisible by 400. 2000 and 2024 are leap years; 1900 and 2100 are not. It only matters in January and February.
learn.numbersBody: The method counts Sunday as 0: Sunday 0, Monday 1, Tuesday 2, Wednesday 3, Thursday 4, Friday 5, Saturday 6. "Sunday = none-day" makes it stick.

practice.level1Blurb: One question per step: anchor, year, month date, answer.
practice.level2Blurb: Practise a single step until it's automatic.
practice.level4Blurb: Stopwatch on. Hints allowed but noted.

slip.leap: Looks like a leap-year slip: in January/February use the 4th/29th in leap years, the 3rd/28th otherwise.
slip.anchor: Looks like the wrong century anchor.
slip.firstEleven: Check the first step of Odd + 11: add 11 only if the last two digits are odd.
slip.secondEleven: Check the second +11: add it only if the half is odd.
slip.noSubtract: Remember to subtract the remainder from 7 before counting forward.
slip.month: Looks like a neighbouring month's doomsday date.
slip.offByOne: One day off — recount the days from the doomsday date.
slip.unknown: Compare with the worked solution below.
